Long Lake #58 First Nation

Long Lake #58 is an Anishinaabe community whose public education accounts connect locally directed schools, language and learning from Elders. These starting sources trace the development of its school system and a dated discussion of educational priorities; they are not a complete community history.

01

Building community-directed schools

The Nation’s education page dates its initial joint education authority with Ginoogaming First Nation to1997 and its independent administration toJuly2012. It describes Migizi Wazisin Elementary School’s development and the later addition of secondary programming at Migizi Miigwanan Secondary School. The account places families, community participation and land-based learning alongside classroom subjects. Its dated plans and old enrolment figures should not be read as a current school census.

Read the sources [1] Long Lake #58 First Nation

02

Education priorities in2025

At a July2025 education summit, Chief Judy Desmoulin and education director Claire Onabigon described learning opportunities extending from early childhood to adult education. Rick Garrick’s report attributes to them an emphasis on student well-being, Elders’ participation, language and a locally developed history curriculum. Onabigon also discussed a proposed language-and-culture department. These are dated participants’ accounts and plans, rather than an independent evaluation or confirmation that every proposal was completed.

Education: Long Lake #58 First Nation Education Authority ↗

The opening Education Authority account traces the jointly established authority, later independent administration and elementary/secondary schools. Selected school descriptions explain community involvement and land-based learning. Some wording anticipates fall2020; staffing and enrolment are not treated as current. Linked agreements and the commissioned mural were not inspected or reproduced.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Read the complete opening Education Authority history and selected Elementary/Secondary School descriptions; staff directories, application links and financial-aid material are outside the substantive review.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Web reader timed out; ordinary direct HTML retrieval returned200 and the selected actual body was read locally. The page warns that the site is under construction. Undated text includes2020 plans; no claim of current staffing, enrolment or completed plans.

Long Lake #58 paving the way for students through education ↗

Publication: 2025-08-05

Rick Garrick reports Chief Judy Desmoulin and education director Claire Onabigon’s July2025 summit presentation about community-directed schools, adult learning and language priorities. Their evaluations are attributed to the speakers. The underlying summit recording, enrolment data and proposed department’s later implementation were not inspected.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Read the complete main article dated August5,2025, including speakers’ attributed accounts and future language/education plans.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026
